newsitem.title: USA: South Africa still needs exchange controls - IMF.
newsitem.headline: South Africa still needs exchange controls - IMF.

text.p: South Africa should continue to improve its standing in financial markets before eliminating exchange controls, a senior official of the International Monetary Fund's African Department said on Saturday.

"The new administration of South Africa has been building up progressively its standing in financial markets and wholesale abolition of the remaining exchange controls on residents before this process is completed and in the absence of a general policy framework may be premature," said Evangelos Calamitsis, director of the IMF African Department.
He said the IMF has supported the gradual elimination of exchange controls for South Africa because liberalization, should proceed when the risk of disruption is minimized.
As long as the South African government implements its medium-term program on a steady basis, it will create an environment conducive to further liberalization, Calamitsis said.

"It will be very important that it is done that way so that one gets the confidence that the liberalization that is occurring is occurring within a very sound, steady macro framework and policy framework," he said.
He also said that the markets should know that South Africa's problems require a comprehensive approach and cohesive action.
"The markets, I don't think, can expect that there will be no damage just simply by removing the controls and taking no action elsewhere. That would be an irrational expectation," he said.

Turning more broadly to Africa, the IMF official said that sub-Saharan Africa could achieve growth of five to six percent next year if it continues to follow sound policies. The IMF projected growth this year at 5.5 percent.
Africa Department officials spoke to reporters at a briefing held in conjunction with the annual meeting of the IMF and and World Bank.
